children: Despite steady investment demand, Bank of America said in a new report Monday that it remains cautious on its outlook for gold prices as physical demand remains weak, expecting prices will be unable to hold above $4K/oz over the next three months.

Although ETF demand has been positive over the last two months, BofA analysts said ETF demand alone cannot keep the market buoyant and could even turn out to be a negative, as weak prices could eventually cause investors to liquidate their positions, adding to selling pressure.

"With the Middle East conflict escalating again, there is a risk that central banks could resume sales," BofA wrote. "Holdings have dipped somewhat, but this is not necessarily surprising, given that ~90% of the increase in the value of gold holdings reflected valuation gains rather than actual purchases."
The bank said the market needs clearer guidance from the Federal Reserve for gold prices to find a bottom and resume their long-term uptrend.

While a dovish shift in the Fed's monetary policy would be a more significant driver for gold, BofA said the metal could also attract renewed bullish momentum if currency debasement fears pick up again.

Gold futures turned lower after touching a ‌one-week high on Monday, pressured by a firmer dollar and higher oil prices, while the market will look to this week's U.S. inflation data - the CPI on Wednesday and PPI on Thursday - as well as comments by Fed Chairman Warsh for more clarity on the Fed's interest rate outlook.

Dollar gains and high oil prices "reinforced concerns that persistent energy-driven inflation could keep the Federal Reserve on a hawkish policy path," Kotak Neo analyst Kaynat Chainwala said in a note.
